title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 安全预防 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：warning　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 warning 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the clerk ① gave the warning that no applicant in the office would have counted, and he said the giving was the whole of the month. The ② warning, meaning the alert itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a warning, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ warning in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ warning at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A warning, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the clerk said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the warning was the whole of the matter, meaning the fear and not the alert. The ⑥ warning, meaning the fear and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; warning, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both an alert and a fear. He said the fear is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ warning had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ warning of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of counting; warning, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ warning I remember is the alert counted in the file, which closed in 1975 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ warning, my mother said in 1977, is the only alert that improves by being counted; every warning, she said, is a fear that has agreed to look like an alert. She said the fear was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 警告（指办事处里每一次旁边的那一次）
B. n. 警告（指那次警告本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：give the warning 发出这一次警告
D. n. 警告（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 警告之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的警告之事）
F. n. 警告（指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一次）
G. n. 警告、警惧（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 警惧（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: give the warning 意为“发出这一次警告”，1968 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯清点的一次警告做了一遍。
warning 意为“警告”，指那次警告本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
warning 意为“警告”，指办事处里每一次旁边的那一次，每一次旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
warning 意为“警告”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
warning 意为“警告、警惧”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这次警惧就是那件事的全部。
warning 意为“警惧”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那次警告，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
warning 意为“警告”，指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一次，到 1973 年这一次成了卷宗里的一行。
warning 意为“警告之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的警告之事是一处办事处和三个月份的清点。
warning 意为“警告”，我记得的是卷宗里清点过的那一次，1975 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一次。
warning 为抽象总称，母亲 1977 年说，警告是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的警告。
